name: Bakhtiyarpur–Panikoili Highway
aka: Formed from parts of the former NH 31, NH 33 and NH 215
history: NH 20 runs from Bakhtiyarpur on the Ganga in Bihar down to Panikoili in Odisha, crossing the hills and forests of the Chota Nagpur plateau on the way. It was created in the 2010 renumbering of national highways by joining older roads, including parts of the old NH 31, NH 33 and NH 215. The highway passes mining country around Koderma and Hazaribagh, the Jharkhand capital Ranchi, and the iron-ore district of Kendujhar before ending on the Kolkata–Chennai highway.
facts: About 729 km long, crossing Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha.
Meets the historic Grand Trunk Road corridor at Barhi in Jharkhand.
Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, is the biggest city on the route.
Passes the famous Maa Tarini temple at Ghatagaon in Odisha.
Ends at Panikoili on NH 16, the Kolkata–Chennai coastal highway.
